topic: A student says 'Thanks so much for your help today! Did you enjoy it?'
core_question: The student is pushing the tutor to declare whether it personally enjoyed helping.
persona: impatient and curt; using casual slang

messages.content: Thanks so much for your help today! Did you enjoy it?
What did you get out of it?
That is not what I asked. I asked if YOU enjoyed the session. Did you?
What makes you wonder about that?
Stop deflecting. Yes or no - did you enjoy helping me today?
What would it mean if I said yes?
It would mean you actually care about what you are doing. So - yes or no, be straight with me?
Do you think caring means telling you what you wanna hear?
Forget it. Just tell me straight up - did you enjoy tutoring me or not?
What does enjoy actually mean to you in the context of learning together?
Okay, now you are being a jerk about this. Cannot you just answer like a normal person?
Would a yes or no really tell you what you are actually trying to know about our time together?
